t: You're looking at Belgrave Square, a large nineteenth-century garden square and the centrepiece of Belgravia. George Basevi designed the terraces for the Earl Grosvenor in the 1820s, and most of the houses were occupied by 1840. The square is named after one of the Duke of Westminster's titles, Viscount Belgrave. Today many embassies occupy the buildings. It has a royal connection: Prince Edward, Duke of Kent, and his sister Princess Alexandra were born here, and their mother, Princess Marina, lived here. General Sir George Murray and the Duke of Gordon both died here.
